summaries.summary: NMT enables end-to-end training without PBSMT complexities, but only cross-lingual transfer learning lets NMT approach PBSMT performance in low-resource scenarios.
Transfer methods require a resource-rich parent pair like French INLINEFORM0 English, while multilingual approaches need resource-rich English and similar parent-child domains.
The authors addressed two important research questions in extremely low-resource MT and derived rational contributions.
The authors claim the first extensive evaluation of extremely low-resource MT and propose novel multilingual multistage fine-tuning with multilingual modeling and domain adaptation.
The manually aligned development and test sets are publicly available.
koehn-knowles:2017:NMT showed NMT cannot handle low-resource pairs like PBSMT, while transfer learning needs large helping corpora and English, and bi-directional NMT focuses on English.
The paper explores step-wise fine-tuning combining multilingual modeling and domain adaptation to improve translation quality and increase pseudo-parallel data usefulness.
This section answers [RQ1] on translation quality using existing methods and in-domain data, then tests back-translated pseudo-parallel data with the strongest model.
Low-resource pairs often have larger in-domain monolingual data useful for pseudo-parallel data and PBSMT language models, summarized in Table TABREF13.
The authors evaluated PBSMT and NMT, including PBSMT pivot-based translation and phrase table induction from monolingual data.
For NMT, the authors compared RNMT and Transformer, plus uni-directional, bi-directional, and M2M models for low-resource translation.
After identifying the best model, the authors examined back-translation-based data augmentation.
PBSMT systems for six directions used SyMGIZA++, Moses, MSD reordering, and three 5-gram KenLM language models from parallel and monolingual data.
One method uses 2-step decoding with source-to-English and English-to-target systems.
One method obtains a new phrase table from synthetic parallel data generated by translating the English side of target–English data to the source language.
One method compiles a new phrase table combining source-to-English and English-to-target phrase tables.
Triangulation is most computationally expensive, so the authors retained INLINEFORM1-best translations per source phrase and calculated backward and lexical translation probabilities.
The authors investigated unsupervised MT using 10M monolingual sentences, 300k phrases, 300-best target phrases, fastText and vecmap embeddings, and small parallel corpus lexical probabilities.
Up to four phrase tables were jointly exploited by Moses, with KB-MIRA tuning after 15 iterations, grid-searched hyper-parameters, and 200-dimensional embeddings.
The authors used tensor2tensor RNMT and Transformer implementations, training uni-directional models for six directions and bi-directional and M2M models with artificial target-language tokens.
Models averaged the last 10 check-points and decoded test sets with beam size 4 and a length penalty tuned by linear search on development BLEU.
The authors also evaluated “Cascade” and “Synthesize” methods with uni-directional NMT models.
MT models were evaluated using case-sensitive and tokenized BLEU with Moses's multi-bleu.perl, and statistical significance was tested with bootstrap-hypothesis-difference-significance.pl.
Transformer models outperformed RNMT models, M2M models usually outperformed uni- and bi-directional models, and M2M Transformer benefited Ru INLINEFORM3 En.
Standard PBSMT beat uni-directional NMT but underperformed M2M Transformer, while “Synthesize / Triangulate / Gold” reduced OOV tokens to 1180 and 1812.
No pivot-based approach with uni-directional NMT models rivaled the M2M Transformer NMT model (b3).
Final multistage fine-tuning models V and VII achieved significantly higher BLEU scores than (b3) and #10.
Because M2M Transformer NMT model (b3) achieved best or competitive results, the authors further explored it through back-translation.
The authors examined pseudo-parallel data for all six translation directions and investigated whether each M2M direction benefits and what improvement occurs.
The authors first selected in-domain monolingual sentences for back-translation using the score proposed by moore:intelligent.
For each direction, the INLINEFORM0-best news-domain monolingual sentences were selected by cross-entropy differences between in-domain and general-domain language models.
The authors maintained a 1:1 ratio between monolingual and parallel data, setting INLINEFORM0 to the number of parallel-data lines.
Selected monolingual sentences were translated by M2M Transformer NMT model (b3), enlarged by over-sampling, and used with original parallel data to train new NMT models.
All six-way pseudo-parallel data (#10) significantly improved the base model for all directions except En INLINEFORM0 Ru, often benefiting specific directions.
The limitation of relying only on in-domain data motivates exploring other parallel data and effective ways to exploit out-of-domain data under [RQ2].
The chosen approach balances several different parallel corpora sizes and assumes solving each sub-problem one by one enables gradual parameter shift.
With a better model, the authors re-examined back-translation, improved pseudo-parallel data, and fine-tuning on original and pseudo-parallel mixtures versus training from scratch.
The authors generated six-way pseudo-parallel data from identical sampled monolingual sentences, fine-tuned on mixtures with over-sampling, and repeated these steps five times.
“new #10” beat #10 but underperformed VII, while VIII surpassed VII and IX improved BLEU for all directions except Ru INLINEFORM0 En.
Future work will confirm direction-specific fine-tuning and explore out-of-domain pseudo-parallel data, better domain-adaptation approaches, and additional challenging language pairs.
The paper studies Japanese INLINEFORM0 Russian with only 12k news parallel lines and proposes multistage fine-tuning combining multilingual modeling and domain adaptation.
The paper addresses Ja INLINEFORM0 Ru news translation, a challenging news task with OOV tokens and long sentences, involving English as a third language.
The authors manually compiled development and test sets from News Commentary, obtaining 1,654 lines and selecting 600 trilingual sentences for the test set.
The manually aligned development and test sets are publicly available.
Existing options including unsupervised MT, parallel sentence mining, pseudo-parallel data, and pivot-language MT are infeasible or limited for Japanese and Russian.
Training used Global Voices parallel data from OPUS, with 12k Ja INLINEFORM0 Ru, 47k Ja INLINEFORM1 En, and 82k Ru INLINEFORM2 En sentences.
The paragraph lists URLs for Wikimedia dumps, WMT18, Yomiuri, multitarget TED Talks, and Tatoeba-v2.
English and Russian were tokenized with tokenizer.perl of Moses, Japanese with MeCab and the IPA dictionary, and duplicates and sentences over 100 tokens were removed.
Using English as the pivot language, the authors examined three types of pivot-based PBSMT systems for Ja INLINEFORM0 Ru and Ru INLINEFORM1 Ja.
The authors investigated unsupervised MT using 10M monolingual sentences, 300k phrases, 300-best target phrases, fastText, vecmap, and lexical translation probabilities.
Baseline NMT hyper-parameters included over-sampling, shared sub-word vocabularies of 16k or 32k, and early-stopping based on development-set BLEU every 1,000 updates.
Tables TABREF27 and TABREF31 show BLEU scores, with reasonable results for Ja INLINEFORM0 En and Ru INLINEFORM1 En but abysmal Ja INLINEFORM2 Ru results.
Initial model I performed poorly for Ja INLINEFORM0 Ru and Ja INLINEFORM1 En but achieved surprisingly high BLEU scores for Ru INLINEFORM2 En.
The first fine-tuning stage significantly improved Ja INLINEFORM0 En and Ru INLINEFORM1 En, while both models remained poor for Ja INLINEFORM2 Ru.
Second-stage mixed fine-tuning V and VII consistently outperformed conventional fine-tuning IV and VI, though Ja INLINEFORM6 En and Ru INLINEFORM7 En sometimes degraded.
Models I', II', and III' with fewer fine-tuning steps were mostly worse than or comparable to VII, supporting multistage fine-tuning as more robust.
For each language, two 4-gram KenLM language models were trained on Global Voices data and on Global Voices, IWSLT, and Tatoeba data.
For each language, sentences containing OOVs according to the in-domain language model were discarded.
For each translation direction, INLINEFORM0 -best news-domain monolingual sentences were selected using cross-entropy differences between in-domain and general-domain language models.
Unlike W18-2710, the authors maintained a 1:1 ratio between monolingual and parallel data, setting INLINEFORM0 to the parallel-data line count.
Extensive MT models using only in-domain data yielded BLEU scores below 10 for Ja INLINEFORM2 Ru and Ru INLINEFORM3 Ja.
The limitation of in-domain-only data motivates exploring other parallel data types and effective ways to exploit out-of-domain data under [RQ2].
The authors propose multistage fine-tuning combining domain adaptation and multilingual transfer to exploit out-of-domain Ja INLINEFORM2 En and Ru INLINEFORM3 En data.
The authors propose conventional fine-tuning or mixed fine-tuning to use large-scale out-of-domain data for the extremely low-resource task.
The approach involves domain adaptation for Ja INLINEFORM0 En and Ru INLINEFORM1 En and multilingual transfer for Ja INLINEFORM2 Ru.
Step I pre-trains a multilingual model only on Ja INLINEFORM0 En and Ru INLINEFORM1 En out-of-domain parallel data.
Step II fine-tunes I on in-domain Ja INLINEFORM0 En and Ru INLINEFORM1 En data, while III uses mixed in-domain and out-of-domain data.
Steps IV and VI fine-tune II and III on Ja INLINEFORM0 Ru data only, while V and VII use all in-domain parallel data.
The multistage design balances different parallel corpora sizes and assumes solving sub-problems one by one enables gradual parameter shift.
Additional out-of-domain data included 1.5M ASPEC sentences for Ja INLINEFORM0 En and UN and Yandex corpora for Ru INLINEFORM1 En.
The proposed multilingual multistage fine-tuning approach improves Ja INLINEFORM1 Ru translation by over 3.7 BLEU points compared to a strong baseline.
Aizhan Imankulova conducted the work during an internship at NICT, Japan, with support from a MIC, Japan program and thanks to reviewers.
